title: The four consumed rows of the settlement step — the agent proposal, the approval at D7.4, the treatment booking and the case move — are in no C row of the plan
source: _work/msr/context/S4.md (ownership rows of S4: two tables, five REST operations, no event, no job, one workflow); Recovery Workbench FSD S4 Litigation and enforcement v3 (A2.13, A2.13.2 integration points, A2.13.3.1, A2.13.3.3); Recovery Workbench Epics 3 to 8 Specification v3 (feature row E5, S4, FEAT-LIT-13); Recovery Workbench TSD S4 Litigation and enforcement v2 (T2, T3.3, T5.2, T6.1, appendix T-A.1); Recovery Workbench Business Rules and Routing Logic v4 (R-LIT-36, R-LIT-37, R-LIT-38); 04 User stories/Recovery Workbench User Stories Epics 3 to 8 v3.md (heading RWB-E5-013, its Data, Endpoints and Permission checks tables)
section: APP s2 Business rationale; s3 Preconditions; s4 Flow steps 3, 6, 7 and 9; s11 Data; s12.2 REST operations consumed; s12.7 Tables owned; s12.8 Contract fakes; s13 Solution plan; s19 Out of scope; CON s2, s3, s7 AC3, s11 Data, s12.2, s12.7, s12.8, s13, s19
description: The legacy story books the treatment inside its own schema and moves the case inside its own process, and it computes nothing on the agent side: AC2 names the agent as the proposer and AC3 names the booking. In the target the four parts of the step belong to four other owners and none of them is in the plan. The proposal with its cost and its effect is P10 rwb-agent's; the approver named by the limit and the approval are P7 rwb-decision's under the DoA matrix; the treatment and its plan are S2 rwb-treatment's, reached on its booking operation; and the case of record and its route state are P3 rwb-case's, reached as a case-move answer on the workflow boundary. The ownership rows of this service list two tables only, legal_action and hearing, and five REST operations, none of which is a proposal, an approval, a booking or a case move; TSD S4 T5.2 names the published Java interfaces of P3, P7, P4, P5 and P6 with no operation, and T-A.1 lists five S4 operations only. Both slices therefore declare the four rows as consumed and faked, write no treatment row, no case row and no column of legal_action on the held path, and record that the metadata contract-dependency row of both slices is None instead of inventing a C row.
evidence: The ownership rows of the context pack give S4 two tables (hearing, legal_action), five REST operations, zero events, zero jobs and one workflow (LitigationWorkflow); FSD S4 A2.13.2 names the integration point as Workbench only and A2.13.3.3 gives the litigation officer as primary with the Head of Litigation and the product head as also-users, so no source names the approval interface; TSD S4 v2 T3.1 defines legal_action (DF-LEG-001 to DF-LEG-014) and hearing (DF-LEG-024 to DF-LEG-029) only, T3.3 gives no treatment or case relationship, T5.2 names the interfaces without an operation, and T-A.1 lists API-S4-001 to API-S4-005 only; the legacy story Data table lists treatment and recovery_case among its five entities and its Endpoints table lists two legal-action operations only; Business Rules and Routing Logic v4 R-LIT-37 books the treatment and names Workbench and ALS core as its systems.
area: Contract and data, S4 rwb-litigation with P10 rwb-agent, P7 rwb-decision, S2 rwb-treatment and P3 rwb-case
owner_role: S4 rwb-litigation service owner with the P10, P7, S2 and P3 owners
proposed: Keep the metadata rows as the plan gives them (H only, C None), build against the four published documents and their fakes on Day 1, and let step D1 decide whether the four rows become C dependencies of this key or the owner stories raise their contract baselines.

title: The trigger of the step, the shape of the agent proposal and the storage of the hold LITIGATION_HELD have no single source, and no source gives a held status value
source: Recovery Workbench FSD S4 Litigation and enforcement v3 (A2.13.1, A2.13.2, A2.13.3.1, A2.13.3.2, A2.13.4.4); Recovery Workbench TSD S4 Litigation and enforcement v2 (T3.1, T3.2, T4); Recovery Workbench Business Rules and Routing Logic v4 (R-LIT-36, R-LIT-37, R-LIT-38, R-LIT-39); 04 User stories/Recovery Workbench User Stories Epics 3 to 8 v3.md (heading RWB-E5-013, its Acceptance criteria and Test cases tables); _work/msr/fragments/RWB-S4-E5013-APP.json and RWB-S4-E5013-CON.json
section: APP s2 Business rationale; s3 Preconditions; s4 Flow steps 1, 4 and 8; s8 Business rules (BR5); s9 State transitions; s11 Data; s12.5 Workflows and activities; s13 Configuration and reference data; s16 Test cases; CON s2, s3, s7 AC1, AC2 and AC5, s11 Data, s12.5, s18
description: Three values of the target shape have no source. First the trigger: the legacy AC1 says the user acts on the screen and the legacy AC2 says the customer or the firm proposes the settlement, while FSD S4 A2.13.2 is a user feature with no background event and A2.13.4.4 declares no system background event at all, so the stories read the arrival as a signal of LitigationWorkflow and declare no event and no Schedule. Second the proposal: R-LIT-36 says the agent proposes the step with its cost and its effect, and no source gives the elements, the types or the format of that proposal, so it is carried as a fact of the rwb-agent answer with the placeholder. Third the hold: R-LIT-37 says to hold the litigation rather than withdraw it, and LOV-LEGAL-STATUS has no held value and legal_action has no hold column, so the hold is read as the stage state LITIGATION_HELD of LitigationWorkflow, answered to rwb-case, with legal_action.status left at FILED and the withdrawal reserved to R-LIT-39; no value is added to the list and no column is added to the table.
evidence: Legacy AC1 gives When the user acts on the screen and AC2 gives When settlement proposed with the rule text the customer or the firm proposes a settlement before judgment; FSD S4 v3 A2.13.2 gives the step rows Opens the screen and settle before judgment with the litigation officer, and A2.13.4.4 is the row None, No background event; TSD S4 v2 T3.2 gives LOV-LEGAL-STATUS as OPEN, FILED, JUDGMENT, ENFORCING, CLOSED, WITHDRAWN with no held value, and T3.1 gives legal_action no hold or offer column; T4 lists R-LIT-36 to R-LIT-38 with the events SETTLEMENT_PROPOSED, SETTLEMENT_APPROVED and SETTLEMENT_REJECTED; Business Rules and Routing Logic v4 R-LIT-37 books the treatment and holds the litigation while R-LIT-39 withdraws the case only when the treatment completes.
area: Workflow, data and contract, S4 rwb-litigation
owner_role: S4 rwb-litigation service owner with the solution architect
proposed: Start the step from the proposal signal, publish the proposal and the hold as declared elements with the placeholder on the fields no source gives, keep LOV-LEGAL-STATUS closed, and let step D1 confirm the trigger and the hold representation.

title: The approver named by the limit has no Litigation role row, and the legacy screen table names SCR-18 for a settlement step whose states it cannot show
source: _work/msr/context/S4.md (architecture v5 slide 3 notes on the DoA matrix); Recovery Workbench FSD S4 Litigation and enforcement v3 (A1.2, A2.13.3.3, Screens); Recovery Workbench TSD S4 Litigation and enforcement v2 (T6.1); Recovery Workbench Business Rules and Routing Logic v4 (R-LIT-36, R-LIT-37, R-LIT-38); 04 User stories/Recovery Workbench User Stories Epics 3 to 8 v3.md (heading RWB-E5-013, its Permission checks, Screen and states and Validation and messages tables)
section: APP s2 Business rationale; s10 Authority; s15 Screens and states; s18 Traceability; s19 Out of scope; CON s2, s3, s7 AC4, s15, s18
description: Two records of the legacy story do not agree with the target. The legacy Permission checks table gives the Litigation capability area the rights C and R only, held by the litigation officer and the enforcement owner, and the FSD A2.13.3.3 names the Head of Litigation and the product head as also-users, while AC1 and R-LIT-36 both send the settlement to an approver named by the limit, at D7.4. That approver is a delegated-authority approver of the DoA matrix and not a role of the Litigation capability area, so the stories consume the approver and the approval from rwb-decision and add no Litigation right for it; the also-users keep the read and approve rights the TSD S4 T6.1 matrix gives them and the approval itself is not a Litigation action. The second record is the screen table: the legacy story lists SCR-18 Notice approval with the states generated, approved, sent, delivered and unserved, none of which is a settlement state, so the step is worked on SCR-19 and SCR-18 is carried read-only as the notice context of the case.
evidence: The legacy Permission checks table gives Litigation C to RW-LITOFF and RW-ENFORCE and Litigation R to a long role list, with no approver row; FSD S4 v3 A2.13.3.3 gives the litigation officer as primary and the Head of Litigation and the product head as also-users; the context pack slide 3 notes state that an approver within their delegated authority (DoA Matrix v2) signs the route decision off, which places the approver outside the capability area; TSD S4 T6.1 gives RW-HEADLIT and RW-PRODHEAD the right RA; Business Rules and Routing Logic v4 R-LIT-36 and R-LIT-37 name the owner as Approver at D7.4 and Restructuring officer, FCR; the legacy Screen and states table lists SCR-19 with pack, instructed, filed, hearing, judgment and SCR-18 with generated, approved, sent, delivered, unserved.
area: Authority and screens, S4 rwb-litigation with P7 rwb-decision
owner_role: S4 rwb-litigation service owner with the P7 rwb-decision owner and the access owner of P4
proposed: Consume the approver and the approval from rwb-decision, add no Litigation right for the approval, keep the also-users as readers and approvers under the DoA matrix, and carry SCR-18 read-only in both stories.
